intent: three new conceptual sheets; single pass per asset; no variants or retries

assets.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: a conceptual hand-drawn illustration sheet for a Naive Zine style public urban-regeneration proposal.
Create ONE landscape PNG with an exact 16:9 canvas, preferably 1920x1080. The layout is EXACTLY four independent complete vignettes in a regular 2x2 arrangement. Imagine invisible vertical and horizontal midlines dividing the canvas in four equal 16:9 quadrants. Center one complete vignette within each quadrant. Each quadrant must be independently crop-safe, with generous cream outer padding and blank space along both center seams; no object, person, line, or scene may cross a seam. NO drawn grid, box borders, panel frames, labels, lettering, logos, brands, numbers, arrows, signs, watermark, legend, UI, or typography anywhere.
Style: friendly specific naïve-zine drawings, thick slightly uneven hand-drawn ink-black #111 outlines, rounded approachable adult people with small dot eyes, restrained flat spot color, modest dry-marker texture, cream paper #F7F4EE everywhere behind the scenes. Bold and readable but airy, generous negative space. Flat ink drawings, not realistic renders. No gradients, shadows, 3D, photos, clip-art sheen, or decorative frame. Use ONLY cream paper, black ink, and the single specified accent color for the entire sheet, with no other hue. Food and skin are cream and black too.
These artworks communicate CONCEPTUAL mechanisms. They are not documentary images, literal site reconstructions, geographic maps, factual architectural surveys, or precise diagrams. Make the requested places symbolic, unbranded, and human-centered. No exact art copying or logo replicas.

Single accent: sky blue #82D6F7.
TOP LEFT: Pike Place-inspired mechanism. One small independent fresh-food stall, a producer talking directly with a shopper, fresh fish and a few baskets of vegetables. Friendly face-to-face exchange is the focal point; a simple awning behind the people, no commercial signage.
TOP RIGHT: Granville-inspired mechanism. A modest food market counter beside an open artisan pottery workshop, a potter shaping a bowl at a wheel, with a tiny theatre entrance suggested by an open doorway and gathered curtain. Everyday people mingle with visitors. Keep all three activities a single compact complete vignette, with no exact recognizable building.
BOTTOM LEFT: Lisbon curation-inspired mechanism. Three visibly different local chefs, each serving a distinctive dish to a few people gathered at ONE long communal table. Simple elegant food-hall feeling through the table and small kitchen counters, no accurate restaurant interior.
BOTTOM RIGHT: Shimonoseki proposal. A Japanese local chef finishing kawara soba noodles on a small roof-tile-shaped platter at a counter, with lemon slices and egg strips represented only by cream and black linework. A visitor meets a fish supplier beside the counter. Include a small friendly pufferfish motif near the supplier's produce crate. Warm personal welcome. No commercial logo or actual restaurant interior.

TOP LEFT: Bilbao-inspired mechanism. People enjoying a modest river promenade and park beside a simple abstract sculptural museum form. A human-scale path connects this compact scene with a few simple city buildings. A conceptual relationship, no specific engineering, geography, or exact landmark reproduction.
TOP RIGHT: Battersea-inspired mechanism. A simple old industrial shell with FOUR tall chimneys, symbolically reused as shops around an inviting public courtyard. A few people stroll and sit together. Keep the four chimneys visible while the small friendly people remain a focus. No exact architectural survey, signs, commercial logos, or recognizable brand.
BOTTOM LEFT: King's Cross-inspired mechanism. A brick railway warehouse with an old industrial roofline, now opening to a student and creative plaza. Adults sketch in notebooks, talk, and sit at a small cafe table. A clear reuse scene, not an exact branded building.
BOTTOM RIGHT: Shimonoseki proposal. An existing modest station building and an adjacent ordinary commercial building, connected by one small shared forecourt. Shoppers and visitors exchange stories face to face in the foreground. Warm scene of reusing and connecting ordinary existing assets. No floorplan, map, arrows, signs, words, or logos.

Warm accessible arrival. The shuttle and ferry are generic conceptual vehicles, not an actual operating route or specific vehicle model. No route arrows or markings.
